title: Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce

seoTitle: Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Smoked wings, tangy Alabama sauce
description: Smoked wings, tangy Alabama sauce. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Chicken wings, split and tips trimmed

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Mayonnaise as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Dry and season wings
steps.instruction: Pat wings completely dry with paper towels — moisture blocks smoke and crisping. Toss with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and brown sugar. Arrange skin-side up on wire racks set over sheet pans with space between each wing so smoke circulates.

steps.title: Smoke low and slow
steps.instruction: Run smoker at 250°F with hickory or oak. Smoke wings 45–60 minutes until the skin looks dry, lightly bronzed, and pulls tight — internal temp at the thickest joint should read 165°F. Avoid saucing now; sugars will burn before the skin crisps.

steps.title: Crisp the skin
steps.instruction: Finish over high heat on the grill (lid open) or under a broiler 3–5 minutes per side until the skin crackles and blisters lightly. Work in batches so wings are not stacked — steam softens skin. Hold crisped wings on a rack, not a closed container.

steps.title: Mix white BBQ sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, cider vinegar, horseradish, lemon juice, Worcestershire, cayenne, and celery seed until smooth. Taste — it should be tangy, creamy, and peppery. Chill 20 minutes if time allows so flavors settle; thin with a splash of vinegar if too thick.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Toss and serve hot
steps.instruction: Toss wings with just enough sauce to coat — add more at the table. Serve immediately on sheet trays with extra sauce and lemon wedges. Hold backup wings uncovered at 200°F up to 20 minutes; do not cover sauced wings or they steam soggy.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Smoked Wings with White BBQ Sauce on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Smoked wings, tangy Alabama sauce. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
